assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Density
items.clue: The mass in each unit of volume of a material.

items.label: Insulating material
items.clue: A substance through which charge cannot flow easily.

items.label: Step-down transformer
items.clue: Lowers the potential difference to a safe value for homes.

items.label: Static electricity
items.clue: Charge that has built up on an object and stays where it is.

questions.stem: The UK mains supply has a frequency of 50 Hz. What does this tell you?

options.text: The pd completes 50 full cycles every minute
The supply frequency is actually 230 Hz
The pd between live and neutral is about 50 V
The pd goes through 50 cycles each second

questions.explanation: Hertz means cycles per second, so a 50 Hz supply completes 50 complete cycles each second.

questions.stem: Why is the insulation covering each wire in a cable colour coded?

options.text: So that each wire can carry a different sized current
Because coloured plastics insulate at a higher voltage
So that each wire can be identified easily
So the colour shows which wire is at the highest pd

questions.explanation: The insulation covering each wire is colour coded for easy identification.

questions.stem: In the equation P = V I, what does each symbol stand for and in which unit is it measured?

options.text: P is power in W, V is pd in V and I is current in A.
P is power in W, V is the pd in A and I is the current in V.
P is power in W, V is pd in ohms and I is current in A.
P is power in J, V is pd in V, and I is current in A.

questions.explanation: These are the quantities and the units the specification gives for P = V I.

questions.stem: A hairdryer has a power of 1500 W. It is switched on for 4 minutes. How much energy does it transfer?
Why is the National Grid an efficient way to transfer energy from power stations to consumers?

options.text: A high pd gives a low current, so less energy is wasted heating the cables.
A high pd makes the energy travel along the transmission cables much faster.
A high pd lowers the resistance of the long cables used in the National Grid.
A high pd increases the power that the power station is able to supply.

questions.explanation: For a given power, raising the pd lowers the current, and the power wasted is I^2 R.

questions.stem: A student rubs a metal rod held in her bare hand with a dry cloth. The rod shows no sign of being charged. Why not?

options.text: The metal was not rubbed hard or long enough to become charged.
Rubbing a smooth metal surface is unable to create any charge.
The rod gains and loses equal numbers of electrons as it is rubbed.
Charge on the rod flows away through her hand and body.

questions.explanation: A metal conducts, so any charge produced does not stay on the rod: it leaks to earth through the student. Charging by rubbing needs an insulating material.

questions.stem: A charged object is moved closer to a second charged object. What happens to the force between them?

options.text: The force gets stronger as the distance between them decreases.
The force stays the same, as it depends only on the two charges.
The force gets weaker, because the two fields start to cancel.
There is no force at all until the two objects touch.

questions.explanation: The second object sits in a field that is stronger closer in, so the force on it increases as the gap closes.

questions.stem: A cube of steel has sides of 0.10 m and a mass of 7.8 kg. What is its density?

options.text: 7800 kg/m³
780 kg/m³
78 kg/m³

questions.stem: What is the job of the live wire in a mains circuit?

options.text: It takes the current back to the supply after the appliance
It carries a current only if a fault develops in the case
It stops the metal case of the appliance becoming live
It carries the alternating potential difference from the supply

questions.explanation: The live wire carries the alternating potential difference from the supply.

questions.stem: A current of 0.60 A flows through a resistor of resistance 12 ohms. What is the power transferred in the resistor?
A food mixer is plugged into a wall socket and switched on. How is energy transferred while it is in use?

options.text: Electrically from the ac mains to the thermal store of the mixer motor.
Electrically from batteries to the kinetic energy of the motor.
Electrically from the ac mains to the kinetic energy of the motor.
From the mains supply to the chemical store of the mixer.

questions.explanation: A mixer is designed to turn a blade, so the useful transfer is to the kinetic energy of an electric motor.

questions.stem: A transmission cable of resistance 5.0 ohms carries a current of 1000 A. What power is wasted in heating the cable?
questions.explanation: P = I^2 R = 1000^2 x 5.0 = 5 000 000 W wasted in heating the cable.
